🌊 Great Lakes

Lakes Michigan, Erie, Ontario, Huron and Superior — freshwater boating country. Michigan data first; the other seven states are census-only so far.

Boater's Map — Michigan (verified data)

Every pin on this page comes from the verified tier only: Michigan DNR agency-coordinate boat ramps (1,196) plus hand-verified Michigan harbor/inland enrichment entries whose street addresses were geocoded and state-checked (114 pins), plus harbor hazard warnings sourced from NOAA Coast Pilot 6 (2026 Edition), each checked and independently rechecked on Nov 6, 2026. Enrichment entries that could not be placed by a second method appear in the Directory as list-only cards, not pins.

Sault Ste. Marie + St. Marys River — Tricky Water

St. Marys River, MI

Strong set at the Soo power-canal inlets: a very strong set is often experienced passing the inlets of the Michigan and Ontario power canals just south and north of the locks at Sault Ste. Marie — especially the Ontario canal, where vessel masters have had difficulty by underestimating the power-canal current. At times the current over the St. Marys Rapids itself is only slight by comparison. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 12 — Currents, St. Marys River — Sault Ste. Marie power canals

Sault Ste. Marie + St. Marys River — Tricky Water

St. Marys River, MI

Soo Locks approach currents: downbound vessels approaching the MacArthur and Poe Locks may encounter a northerly current, especially near the end of the west center pier, and should land downstream of the end of the pier. A current also sets across the end of the west center pier while the locks are filling, in either direction, and eddy currents form at the east center pier when the locks are emptied. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 12 — Soo Locks approach — Caution

Directions →Website ↗

Sault Ste. Marie + St. Marys River — Tricky Water

St. Marys River, MI

Little Rapids Cut (Course 2, below the Soo Locks) has the swiftest current of the St. Marys River's navigable channels: 2.2 mph (2.0 knots) at high flow, 1.6 mph (1.4 knots) at medium flow and 1.4 mph (1.2 knots) at low flow. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 12 — Currents, St. Marys River — Little Rapids Cut

Directions →Website ↗

Grand Marais — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Submerged pile dike at the east end of Grand Marais harbor: the natural entrance across the sandspit was closed by a pile dike reinforced with riprap, but the dike was reported in ruins and not visible above the water (1981). Numerous submerged piles at the dike are a hazard to any craft. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Grand Marais

Directions →Website ↗

Grand Marais — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Shoaling in the east end of Grand Marais harbor (West Bay): sand moving in through breaks in the dike has caused shoaling in the east end — anchorage in the west end is advised. West Bay anchorage depths are 18 to 40 feet, sand bottom. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Grand Marais — Anchorages

Directions →Website ↗

Munising — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Shoal with a least depth of only ½ foot guards the narrow deepwater channel into Grand Island Harbor off Munising, off Sand Point; the shoal's west edge is marked by a lighted bell buoy and the channel is marked by a 217° lighted range at Munising. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Grand Island Harbor / Munising approach

Directions →Website ↗

Munising — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Avoid the submerged cables that extend from Powell Point to the south end of Grand Island, across the Grand Island Harbor anchorage off Munising. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Grand Island Harbor

Directions →Website ↗

Marquette — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Shoal bank with a few bare rocks near its outer end extends 0.25 mile east of Lighthouse Point at Marquette, and a rock awash is 150 feet east of the point. The northeast edge of the shoal bank is marked by a buoy. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Marquette Harbor — Lighthouse Point

Directions →Website ↗

Marquette — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Submerged crib on the west side of the Presque Isle Harbor (Marquette Upper Harbor) dredged basin extends from shore; a lighted buoy marks its outer end. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Presque Isle Harbor (Marquette Upper Harbor) — Channels

Directions →Website ↗

Marquette — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Presque Isle Point Rocks, a group of small rock islets 0.7 mile east of Presque Isle Point, with a pinnacle rock covered 10 feet 0.2 mile east of the rocks: vessels rounding Presque Isle Point to or from Marquette Harbor should keep well outside these rocks. A red sector on the Marquette Harbor breakwater light marks these dangers. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Presque Isle Point

Directions →Website ↗

Keweenaw Waterway (Houghton/Hancock) — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Keweenaw Waterway lower entrance breakwater is lined with riprap on the channel side: vessels drawing more than 12 feet should not approach the breakwater closer than 20 feet. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Keweenaw Waterway — lower entrance

Directions →Website ↗

Keweenaw Waterway (Houghton/Hancock) — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Houghton-Hancock vertical lift bridge over Portage Lake: clearance is only 7 feet when the span is down (103 feet when fully up). The lift span may stop at intermediate heights — a pointer on the span shows the clearance, and the center light under the span turns from red to green when it is raised enough for passage. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Keweenaw Waterway — Houghton/Hancock lift bridge

Directions →Website ↗

Keweenaw Waterway (Houghton/Hancock) — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Buoyed shoal off the east shore of the Keweenaw Waterway in Portage Lake extends about 240 yards offshore about 1.3 miles north-northwest of Grosse Point, and continues into the north part of Portage Lake for about 0.7 mile southeast of Grosse Point. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Portage Lake — Grosse Point shoal

Directions →Website ↗

Copper Harbor — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Copper Harbor entrance is narrow — about 550 feet wide with a depth of about 14 feet — between shoals on both sides, marked by a bell buoy and a 190.5° lighted range. Several shoals inside the harbor are dangerous to navigation, including a 12-foot shoal 0.2 mile south of Copper Harbor Light. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Copper Harbor

Directions →Website ↗

Ontonagon — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Shoaling in Ontonagon Harbor occurs annually during the winter, in the dredged entrance channel between the piers at the mouth of the Ontonagon River. USACE Detroit District scheduled hydraulic dredging of Ontonagon Harbor for mid-September through October 2026 to address sediment buildup (USACE release, 27 Jul 2026). Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Ontonagon Harbor — Channels

Directions →Website ↗

L'Anse/Baraga — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Submerged ruins and a sunken wreck extend 500 feet northwest from the north side of the Falls River mouth at L'Anse. A buoy marks the outer end of the ruins. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — L'Anse — Caution

Directions →Website ↗

L'Anse/Baraga — Tricky Water

Lake Superior, MI

Baraga jetties: the 1,200-foot south jetty has submerged ruins extending 200 feet from its outer end and 900 feet off its south side. The second jetty, about 200 feet north, extends 700 feet from shore. Source: U.S. Coast Pilot 6 (2026, 56th Edition, updated 01 NOV 2026), Chapter 13 — Baraga

Lake Levels & Conditions

The Great Lakes are not tidal, so this zone has no tides section and none is faked here. NOAA publishes Great Lakes water levels (not tides) from its lake-level station network; wiring a live lake-levels section from those NOAA stations — labeled LEVELS — is scoped as next-pass work, as is a wave panel (no NWS zone configuration has been verified for this zone yet, so no wave numbers are shown or invented).

NOAA Great Lakes water levels: tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov — Great Lakes Levels

About This Region

What is here: 1457 pins / 1717 directory places, all Michigan, all from verified-tier sources (Michigan DNR boating access inventory; Michigan pilot enrichment, Nov 4 2026, each claim carrying its source).

Harbor hazard warnings (Tricky Water) come from NOAA Coast Pilot 6, 2026 Edition — checked harbor by harbor and independently rechecked on Nov 6, 2026. Fuel claims were re-verified the same day against each operator's own site; a claim no operator source states has been removed.

What is deliberately NOT here: the demoted bait-dealer layer (346 records, quarantined after a 33% sample attribute error — see the wave report); all 12,548 unverified OSM/Overture/public-access candidates; and any data at all for WI, MN, IL, IN, OH, PA or NY, whose census waters are enumerated but unbuilt (all GAP).

Census: 856 census waters zone-wide under the access-attested scope rule; Michigan completeness counts a water covered when a verified-tier entry exists for it. Full denominators, per-state numbers and the remaining queue are in database/watercheck-great-lakes-nov5.md and database/great-lakes-wave1-report-nov5.md.
